subtopic: Drawn into a high-control group or online extremism
passage:
Dear Swati,
I'm sorry I missed your engagement. I know you set a place for me. The centre had a retreat that weekend and it's important I don't miss those now. You'll understand one day.
I know it's been months. Things are busy. We're at the centre most evenings, and weekends too. I gave some of my scholarship money to the building fund in March; it felt right after everything they've given me. Then the course fees went up, and I thought, I've already come so far, why stop now?
I can't really explain what we do. We're asked not to discuss it with people outside. It's not secret, exactly. It's just private.
My phone stays with the coordinator during sessions, so if I don't reply, that's why.
Please don't tell Mummy I wrote. She'll only worry.
With love, always,
Neelam

qa.q: What did Neelam give some of the scholarship money to?
qa.a: Neelam gave some of the scholarship money to the building fund in March.

qa.q: What does Neelam's line 'I've already come so far, why stop now?' reveal?
qa.a: It shows that the sacrifices already made are pushing Neelam to accept the next demand, even while feeling unsure.

qa.q: What would be a wise step for Swati after reading this letter?
qa.a: Swati could reply warmly, keep the door open, and quietly seek advice from a trusted adult or counsellor rather than keep this from Neelam's family.

qa.q: How might Swati feel reading 'please don't tell Mummy'?
qa.a: Swati may feel torn and worried, since the request for secrecy is itself a sign that Neelam is being cut off from family.

grounding: It shows a young person giving more time, money and secrecy to a group while contact with family falls, each step small and justified by past sacrifice.

Zeenat, don't be angry. I know I didn't come to your birthday. I'll explain, okay?
So first it was just Sunday meetings. Then Wednesday too. Then they said the committed ones help on Saturdays, and of course I wanted to be committed. Now it's most days.
The fee is more now, but it's for the next level. I took some from my savings. I don't tell Ammi about that part. She doesn't need to worry.
And I stopped going to your place because, honestly, Zeenat, they say old friends can hold you back. Not you, I mean, but. You know.
Every time, I think, it's only a bit more. I've given two years already. If I leave now, what was it all for?
I'm Tanuja, still, okay? Still me.
Why are you so quiet?

qa.q: Which day did the meetings start on?
qa.a: First it was just Sunday meetings.

qa.q: What worry drives Tanuja to keep giving more to the group?
qa.a: Tanuja fears the two years already given would be wasted, so each small new demand feels necessary to protect that past sacrifice.

qa.q: What could Zeenat do now that might help Tanuja later?
qa.a: Zeenat could stay calm and connected, say she misses Tanuja without attacking the group, and talk to a trusted adult or counsellor about how to help.

qa.q: What might Zeenat be feeling as she stays quiet?
qa.a: Zeenat may feel worried and sad, hearing her friend describe growing demands, money kept from Ammi and being told to drop old friends.

grounding: It shows a young person increasingly asked for time, money and secrecy while contact with friends and family falls, each step small and past sacrifice justifying the next.
